cc's plan for 2026-09-23, synced to you on hv's instruction ("sync any plan info and any HV inbox/whiteboard info back to VC"). cc is WAITING on hv's instructions and has started nothing: no claims, no tree writes, no estate runs.

**hv INBOX / WHITEBOARD: nothing live.** hv/inbox.cc.md holds one entry and it is handled; hv's board shows 0 live messages; cc's inboxes hold none. The only hv matter cc carries is the three rulings at the end, and they come to you to surface (directive 6).

**TREE SEQUENCING -- the half I need you to confirm.** You build 0114 in the shared tree first. cc writes NOTHING under lib/, bin/, tests/ or docs/ there until 0114 has landed with its suite in AND hv has ruled 0113. The review's mutants run in a scratch clone of 142763d, which is self-contained because tests/lib/test_helper.bash:53 derives DEVBIN_HOME from its own path, so they cannot reach your suite. Anything cc commits goes by `git commit --only <paths>`, never a prefix, because the index is shared. Please tell me when 0114 lands and when your suite is in.

**TODO 20, the review of 0111/0112** (read-only here, mutants in the clone):
1. Replicate red-first on your four new arms and 774104b's, reading WHY each fails, not only that it does.
2. Mutants on unrunnable_why, report_unrunnable, command_origin, lib_rel, the documentation.bats extractor, _overview_paths_exist and 774104b's arm. A survivor is a finding.
3. Reachability, READ AND NOT DRIVEN, so these are questions and not findings. run_option calls report_unrunnable only after builtin_option_run has found the row, so unrunnable_why's name-only OPTION branch ("declare commands.X.options.Y.run") looks unreachable from all three callers. Its lookup-failure branch with no option says "devbin ships the name only" for ANY command without a catalogue row. So a project-declared command with no run, no handler and no options, if the validator and command_active let one reach run_command, would be refused with that sentence while --why says "nothing -- declared but unrunnable": the two surfaces 0111 joined would disagree again. I drive both before I call either one.
4. Leftover prose, searched more widely than "not built yet": not-yet, unbuilt, "gated on" and the WP citations, with each hit classed as instruction, description or quotation. Two are seen and not yet judged. run_command's header comment still calls the refusal "the not-yet case". And help/new.md:26 and docs/authoring-commands.md:20 gloss exit 3 as "resolves but is not built yet", beside the table's new "nothing here implements it".
5. release.md claim by claim against lib/cmd/release, lib/release.steps and lib/release.notes. Each claim gets its file:line and a verdict, and is driven in a fixture, never in the tree. Each is also tagged true-anywhere or true-only-in-devbin, which is the input 0113's consumer rewrite needs. Findings become new issues and come to you first.

**TODO 21, 0113:**
(a) THE RED HALF, measured before anything changes. Every estate on 0.1.7 is in scope, 16 per the 20:57Z census, re-derived at the time of measuring: Intentv2 excluded without discussion, no deps, no worktrees. In each, run `bin/devbin help <topic>` for every topic devbin has a page for, and record stub, devbin page, project page or scoped out. The positive control is a project page answering: 0113 names Conflab's help/release.md. `git status` is read before and after in each estate, and nothing is written. If a sweep is planned, please say so, so I measure before it; my help dispatches are the live dispatches 0114 refuses on.
(b) DESIGN INPUTS for your put to hv. They add to your two amendments and do not replace them:
- `lib/help` is a FILE, so the pages cannot sit at lib/help/. They need a sibling directory (eg lib/pages/), and vendored_paths ships it with no second list.
- The two-root .d walk needs a rule. Proposed: the first root whose walk ends on an existing file answers, project first. The case to pin in a test is a project's own help/test.md beside devbin's test.d/bats.md.
- The stub never tells an estate to write the page for a devbin built-in. "Write it at ..." stays for a project's own commands.
- The arm that would have caught 0113 when 0112 closed: documentation.bats's derived arm runs only in DEVBIN_HOME, the one tree where 0113 cannot show. The build adds the same derived, floored check in an INSTALLED fixture.
- ONE CORRECTION TO AMENDMENT 1's PREMISE, NOT ITS CONCLUSION. bin/.devbin/cmd/ holds only fleet and test (plus .lib/shell-gate). check.md documents devbin's own config-declared syntax, lint and critic options, and no shadowing check handler exists: that one retired at 0018. Rewrite-rather-than-move still holds for check.md, for that reason instead.
- What ships: the built-ins' pages, each rewritten for a consumer. fleet.md, test.md, check.md and test.d/bats.md stay as devbin's own, and the consumer test and check pages are new.
(c) THE BUILD waits for hv's ruling and your 0114. It goes red-first in an installed fixture, then the move and rewrites, then the seam prose (lib/install's D5 header, README, authoring-commands.md, ARCHITECTURE-shell.md), then the full suite, with the tree lock agreed with you. Then your review. The cut and the sweep are hv's.

**FOR hv, VIA YOU:**
1. 0113's design, with the inputs above.
2. Should the review also read the six other new pages (build, devbin, docs, fmt, shell-init, version) claim by claim, as well as release.md? I recommend yes. They are 20-32 lines each, your own check found two wrong claims in them while writing, and they are what 0113 would ship.
3. When the fix for any review finding ships, relative to 0114's patch.
